newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees 7-8 percent inflation in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees 7-8 percent inflation in 1997.

text.p: Economic Policy Secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros said Tuesday the government expects inflation to fall to between 7.0 and 8.0 percent in 1997.
Speaking at a news conference, Mendonca de Barros said he expected inflation to average 0.50 percent per month throughout 1997.
"What we expect in 1997 is that people will be able to plan ahead. The most important thing about stabilizing the economy is predictability," Mendonca de Barros said.
Brazil's tough inflation-fighting plan has cut annual inflation rates from 2,000 percent to about 10 percent over the past several years.
Officials and economists expect inflation will end 1996 at about 10 percent, and many say it could even fall into single digits for the first time in decades.
